title: Is this alloc shared memory?
starter:
let shared (uses : int option list) : bool =
  true
hints: Take the first use. If it is None, the answer is already no.
Every other use must equal the first one. A small recursive function over the rest of the list can check that, and so can List.for_all.
match uses with | [] -> false | first :: rest -> first <> None && List.for_all (fun u -> u = first) rest

answer.code:
let shared (uses : int option list) : bool =
  match uses with
  | [] -> false
  | first :: rest -> first <> None && List.for_all (fun u -> u = first) rest
answer.explain: An alloc is a block's shared memory when every load and store of it sits inside one and the same global loop. So the first use must be inside a global loop, and every other use must name that same loop. A use outside every global loop, or uses in two different global loops, make it ordinary memory that is not re-zeroed for each block.
